summary: Germany's largest labor union IG Metall and automaker Volkswagen are holding wage negotiations, as the company looks to embark on cost-cutting measures. Meanwhile, Germany's president is in Ghana.

summary: According to a study by the Körber Foundation, a growing number of Germans now oppose providing military aid to Ukraine. The majority also believes that Germany should take a neutral position between the US and China.

summary: A Human Rights Watch report found that Modi's rule in India has eroded the rule of law and "systematically weakened institutions" meant to protect freedoms. Also, in Delhi a man injured nine police with a knife.

summary: Bharatiya Janata Party and Shiromani Akali Dal have announced their alliance for the upcoming 2027 assembly elections. High drama in TN ahead of deepam lighting: TN BJP chief, other Hindu leaders detained
summary: Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran faced house arrest while attempting to attend the Karthigai Deepam festival. Police enforced strict restrictions and detained several BJP leaders and Hindu groups across the state. The Madurai district administration banned public gatherings to ensure law and order during the event.

headline: 'I want Brezza': Cop cancels wedding for not getting preferred car in dowry, suspended
summary: A controversial incident involving a Delhi Police constable, Kuldeep, has led to his suspension after his wedding was reportedly derailed by dowry demands. The bride's family claimed that he insisted on receiving a Maruti Suzuki Brezza, diverging from their agreement, which led to an altercation. Ultimately, he returned with a large group to leave the bride stranded at the mandap.

headline: Shepherds from Rajasthan trek 2,000km to Maharashtra for grass, return without luck
summary: A herd of 12,000 sheep and 25 camels has faced severe drought conditions in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region. Herders from Rajasthan, generally welcomed, are transporting their livestock back due to extreme fodder shortages. Local farmers typically benefit from the herds due to manure and natural fertilization provided by the animals.

headline: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO, but it won't be like last time
summary: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO, but the job he returns to has changed. The board that pushed him out over his lack of candour reinstated him after he disclosed more affairs and the White House lobbied. With a new chair, a national security committee, an open investigation into Megaspeed and Chinese intelligence claims, and congressional hearings ahead, Huang's second run comes with far more scrutiny than his first.

headline: LA couple wins $7.65M, landlord used fake ICE uniforms to scare tenants
summary: Andrew and Brigid Elrod won $7.65 million after a Los Angeles jury found their Koreatown landlord, K3 Holdings, had harassed and retaliated against them for organising tenants. A former company manager testified that its principal suggested using fake ICE uniforms to frighten Latino residents into leaving. The couple moved out in 2023 after repeated eviction threats.

headline: Deepathoon row: One lamp, one night. Has Tamil Nadu done it right?
summary: Supreme Court has allowed the lamp to be lit once on Nov 24 at Thiruparankundram, but leaves questions of worship and access open. State should argue those issues at the Jan hearing instead of spending public money on a review of the interim order.

headline: US delays 60 Patriot missiles for Ukraine as Russia intensifies attacks
summary: Ukraine faces considerable setbacks in obtaining and deploying Patriot missile interceptors from the US, with these essential systems already funded by its Western allies. Reports suggest that approximately 60 interceptors await authorization, a pressing concern as Russian missile strikes intensify. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has underscored the urgent need for these missiles to shield Ukrainian urban centers, particularly with winter looming, amplifying the necessity of robust air defense for critical infrastructure.

headline: 'Teams were playing out Bumrah': Pathan on how Arshdeep's MI arrival changes things
summary: In a bold maneuver, Mumbai Indians have traded Hardik Pandya to secure the talents of Arshdeep Singh from Punjab Kings. Just in time for the IPL 2027 auction, this strategic acquisition is poised to enhance MI's already formidable bowling attack, with many experts touting a potentially game-changing synergy between Arshdeep and Jasprit Bumrah.

headline: An Australian woman's Doberman fell nearly six metres into an abandoned mineshaft
summary: In a remarkable rescue in Western Victoria, a Doberman named Magic plummeted nearly six metres into an abandoned mineshaft while pursuing a rabbit. Thankfully, the Fire Rescue Victoria's high-angle rescue team managed to pull her out unharmed. This isn't the first time for her owner, as another of their dogs had a similar mishap years ago.

headline: Tiny 4.77-gram turtle released in Perth grows to 100 grams in first survival proof
summary: A juvenile southwestern snake-necked turtle, previously incubated in a lab and released, was recaptured during a survey. This turtle demonstrated significant weight gain since its release, showcasing the success of a conservation program. The population of this species around Perth has been declining due to predation and habitat loss.

headline: $400,000 Walmart heat settlement clears first court hurdle
summary: A federal court in San Diego has approved a $400,000 settlement for Walmart's El Centro store workers. The settlement aims to compensate hourly employees exposed to high temperatures from June 2018 to April 2026. Class attorneys may request up to $133,333 in fees while the complainant seeks a potential $10,000 award.

headline: Video: Bengaluru woman dies after boyfriend pushes her during argument at lodge
summary: In a tragic incident, a 23-year-old woman named Aishwarya lost her life following a dispute with her friend Santhosh at a lodge. The two had been drinking, which intensified their conversation about trust. During the altercation, Aishwarya threatened to take her own life.

'Breaking the door down': Ex-cricketer hails Priyansh Arya after record-breaking 181

His incredible innings featured 19 sixes, tying the world record for T20 sixes in one match. With his standout performances in the IPL and significant contributions to India A, calls for his inclusion in the national team are growing.

His comments, including the remark "Tawaifs have more shame than your bahus", drew sharp criticism from SP, Congress and BJP leaders, who accused him of making derogatory statements about women.

headline: 'Not everyone did it': Hughes hits back at Lehmann's 150-year ball-tampering claim
summary: Merv Hughes has expressed disagreement with Darren Lehmann's statements regarding the long history of ball-tampering in cricket. He emphasised that the practice was not prevalent during his playing days or as a selector. Hughes noted that former players trying to justify past actions are problematic in their claims.

He noted that these leaders are already reaching out to BJP officials in both Delhi and Uttar Pradesh. This trend of political shifts intensifies as elections approach, which is evident with past defections.

headline: LeT, JeM proxies exposed, ISI eyes revival of 19 dormant terror outfits in J&K

The strategy could involve reconnecting with former militants, recruiting local youth and rebuilding networks to evade investigations. The revived outfits may also be used for propaganda and disinformation campaigns.

headline: Karthigai Deepam: Security tightened at two lighting spots on Thiruparankundram hill

Protective temporary structures will be erected to maintain the sanctity of the site. Only those with proper authorization will enter, and a standby team of medical and fire personnel will ensure a safe and secure environment throughout the festivities.

summary: Delhi's cycling safety is compromised by parked vehicles and wrong-way driving, according to a recent study. summary: India dominates airborne anti-submarine warfare with the Boeing P-8I Poseidon, which offers advanced capabilities and technology. In a conversation with Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi about her book ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, she recalled raising concerns over his safety, including during a Bihar tour. The society failed to pay interest after June 2024, constituting a clear deficiency in service. The complainant, Gangadharaiah, sought higher interest rates and compensation for mental agony.

headline: Rising toll: Why Delhi continues to struggle with road safety
summary: Fatal road accidents in Delhi saw a significant increase by 7.7% compared to the same period last year. The total number of accidents rose by 13% from the previous year, highlighting alarming trends. Key factors contributing to these accidents include speeding and inadequate road infrastructure, according to officials.

headline: Priyansh Arya rewrites history, breaks KL Rahul's record for highest T20 score
summary: Priyansh Arya, the captain of Delhi, delivered an extraordinary performance in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy by scoring 181 runs. His remarkable innings featured an incredible 19 sixes, breaking KL Rahul's previous record for a T20 innings. Delhi finished strong, amassing a total of 275 runs for five wickets, moving Arya to second place in the highest individual scores of men's T20 cricket, marking a significant moment in T20 history.

headline: China's Shenzhou-24 carries Pakistan's first astronaut into space
summary: A new Chinese crew is on its way to the Tiangong station after a launch that China called a complete success. This includes a Pakistani pilot, who is making a brief visit.

headline: PM Shehbaz takes notice of provocative statements by cabinet members, urges them to settle differences amicably
summary: ISLAMABAD: Amid rising political tensions, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday took notice of provocative statements by the federal cabinet members against each other and directed them to resolve their differences through consultation. The remarks come amid a war of words between coalition partners over the past few days regarding a proposed referendum on the creation of new provinces, with a federal cabinet member publicly expressing his grievances against a colleague.

headline: Plea filed in LHC against alleged 'siege' of Fazl's residence in Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A plea challenging the alleged “siege” of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence in Punjab’s provincial capital was filed in the Lahore High Court on Tuesday. The petition, filed by JUI-F lawyer Advocate Abrar Hussain, has yet to be fixed. In his petition, the lawyer alleged that around 3,000 police personnel had been deployed outside Fazl’s residence, effectively confining him to his house.

headline: Imran wants PTI to expand political alliance, extend outreach to Fazl and other opposition parties, core committee told
summary: ISLAMABAD: The PTI’s core committee has been informed that incarcerated party founder Imran Khan wanted it to expand its “political alliance” and extend outreach to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties. Imran’s instructions were conveyed to the committee during an overnight meeting that began on Monday and during which lawyer Latif Khosa briefed the members on his meeting with Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, at the Adiala jail earlier this month.

headline: PM Shehbaz congratulates CDF Munir on Hall of Fame induction at Malaysia’s National Defence Studies Centre
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday congratulated Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on his induction into the Hall of Fame at Malaysia’s National Defence Studies Centre. “This distinction also reflects the enduring friendship between Pakistan and Malaysia,” the premier said on X. “Field Marshal’s resolute leadership during Marka-i-Haq, unwavering commitment to national defence, invaluable contributions to promoting peace, and enhancing Pakistan’s standing internationally makes this honour truly befitting,” he added.

headline: PTI moves IHC for live broadcast of Al-Qadir Trust case hearing
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has filed a petition in the Islamabad High Court (IHC), seeking live broadcast of the appeal proceedings in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case involving party founder Imran Khan. Imran and his wife, Bushra Bibi, were convicted and sentenced in January 2025 in the corruption case.

headline: Cricket's saliva ban to stay despite Indian skipper Shubman Gill’s call to overturn rule
summary: The International Cricket Council has no plans to reverse the ban on applying saliva to shine the ball, despite India skipper Shubman Gill’s call to allow the practice again. Gill on Monday said the ban should be revoked to help bowlers get reverse swing, after India’s high-scoring opening Test in Wellington against New Zealand ended in a draw.

headline: Collision between bus, truck kills 11 in UAE
summary: Eleven people were killed when a bus and a truck collided in Ras Al Khaimah in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), authorities in the Gulf nation said on Tuesday. “Investigations into the circumstances and causes of the accident are ongoing,” the Ministry of Interior stated on its X account. According to the ministry, emergency teams were dispatched to the accident site immediately after receiving the report.

headline: Tech firms soar as Huang’s return reinvigorates AI trade
summary: Technology firms rocketed Tuesday as Asia joined a global stock surge following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia boss less than two weeks after stepping down over extramarital affairs including with an alleged Chinese spy. The Silicon Valley giant’s resignation on November 12 sent shockwaves through markets and dealt a severe blow to the AI trade, which was already under pressure amid worries over profitability and the vast sums pumped into the sector.

headline: Petroleum dealers warn of another strike over unmet demands
summary: KARACHI: The Paki­stan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) on Monday warned that dealers would shut their petrol pumps unless the government fixes fuel prices for 30 days at a time, giving it 15 days to resolve the issue. This is the latest of several strike calls by fuel retailers this year; on each previous occasion, the call was withdrawn after the government stepped in. This time too, dealers say, the issues they raised earlier remain unresolved.

headline: Punjab holds over 60pc of senior federal posts, Senate body told
summary: ISLAMABAD: Punjab holds 60.17 per cent of senior posts in the Federal Secretariat, a Senate subcommittee was told on Monday, prompting a sharp demand for immediate rectification and strict enforcement of the constitutional shares of all provinces in federal employment and natural resources.

headline: Challan submitted in Hina Javed murder case
summary: RAWALPINDI: Police have submitted challan to the District Prosecution Branch in the murder case of Hina Javed after completing the investigation and incorporating forensic reports into the case record. The district prosecutor has received the challan and initiated scrutiny. Sources said it could not be submitted on Saturday due to unavailability of the district prosecutor.

headline: Used phone import surge hits industry
summary: ISLAMABAD: Imports of used smartphones surged from 1,434 units in July to 98,383 in October, as the duty gap between locally manufactured phones and imports narrowed. The country recorded 150,133 arrivals, including 51,750 new smartphones valued at $71.7 million in October, compared with 18,431 smartphones valued at $17.8m in July.

headline: LHC rejects US-Indian origin citizen’s plea for Pakistan Origin Card
summary: LAHORE: Dismissing a petition by an American citizen of Indian origin, the Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that marriage to a Pakistani citizen does not create an automatic right to seek a Pakistan Origin Card (POC). The petition says Dr Talha Muadh Ghulam Jilani, formerly Dr Jaysinha Shamrao Shinde, embraced Islam in 1990 and renounced Indian nationality before taking American citizenship in 2007.

headline: Digital gateway launched in Sindh for youth to access banking, education and jobs
summary: Under Sindh Youth Card, govt, financial organisations and private sector will provide support system to young people, says Murad. Registration begins across all 30 districts to select 100,000 young people in first phase; initiative to be expanded to one million. KARACHI: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah has described the Sindh Youth Card as a landmark youth empowerment initiative designed to connect young people with education, employment, financial inclusion, skills development and entrepreneurship opportunities through a single digital platform.

headline: Liberté, égalité, fatigué—the young are tired of everyone

When the day finally arrived, a perfect storm swept across France, from its largest metropolitan areas to its mid-sized towns.

headline: Huang’s Nvidia return sparks relief for battered AI trade, but questions remain
summary: Huang’s reinstatement atop the semiconductor giant halted a slide in technology shares that had sent the benchmark S&P 500 into a correction, though there was also some caution that his second coming may raise new risks for the company and industry.

headline: Plan to split gas firms lands on PM’s table
summary: Framework proposes breaking up both companies into six to eight entities. Separate transmission, distribution and sales businesses envisaged to create competitive gas market; IMF backs reforms. Over Rs3tr in gas circular debt to be shifted to special purpose vehicle; domestic tariffs may rise.

headline: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza
summary: CAIRO/JERUSALEM: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three people in Gaza on Monday, including a man working for the UN Palestinian refugee agency UNRWA, the relief age­ncy and local health officials said. The UNRWA worker, whom medics named as Adel Al-Helo, was working near a well in the Jabalia refugee camp in the enclave’s north, the agency and medics said. Three others were wounded in the strike, they said.

headline: Walkout over withdrawal of Fazl’s security
summary: QUETTA: Opposition members in the Balochistan Assembly staged a walkout on Monday to protest against the withdrawal of security guards provided to JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman. They later returned to the house after provincial ministers intervened and persuaded them to end their protest. The assembly session was presided over by a member of the Panel of Chairmen Dr Ashok Kumar.

headline: The missing link
summary: Months after it first emerged, the bang is still more noise than a clarion call of reason. Support — strong on rhetoric but weak on evidence — comes mainly from ministers and friendly analysts. One minister cites Afghanistan’s 34 units.

headline: 'Free' land and thriving businesses: French village defies rural decline
summary: As France's mayors gather in Paris for their annual convention, the decline in living standards and public services in both urban and rural areas is high on the agenda. Rural mayors, in particular, are concerned about the shrinking populations of their communities.

headline: Moldova launches national preparedness campaign after drone incursions
summary: Moldova is urging its citizens to prepare for emergencies as the war in neighbouring Ukraine brings new risks across its border. The “Moldova Ready” campaign, launched in Chisinau, includes a display of the remains of a drone carrying 52kg of explosives after it crashed in the country last month. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

headline: Top Spanish court closes case against Catalan separatist leader
summary: Spain's Supreme Court has applied a controversial amnesty law to former Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, closing criminal proceedings against him over his role in the region's failed 2017 independence bid. The ruling, which comes ahead of a snap general election on Sunday, marks the final step in the implementation of the amnesty law, passed by parliament in 2024.

headline: Iranian family seeks release of twin sisters facing death penalty and 25 years in prison
summary: Twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi are awaiting their sentences in Iran. They were arrested in January 2026, at the age of just 19, for taking part in protests against the Iranian regime. Taraneh is facing the death penalty, while Romina has been sentenced to 25 years in prison.

headline: Russian casualties in Ukraine war: New reports suggest death toll as high as 700,000
summary: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests some 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency.

headline: Iowa: Toxic dust fears as US Army blows up 10,000 pounds of explosives
summary: An enormous explosion rang out across rural Iowa Tuesday as the US military carried out the controlled detonation of some 10,000 pounds of lead azide. US officials say the material, which was once used as a detonator in munitions, had become unstable and was at risk at risk of spontaneous explosion.

headline: Long waits 'a tragedy' as thousands seek ADHD and autism assessments
summary: A GP warns that long waits for ADHD and autism assessments mean those most in need are not being seen.

headline: Trump slaps new tariffs on 14 nations; India faces additional 17%
summary: Rejecting claims of surplus capacity in any sector, the Indian government emphasises its commitment to forging a strong bilateral trade agreement with the US. Recent tariff negotiations hit a snag following a US Supreme Court ruling, temporarily halting progress. However, prior to this, an accord on extra tariffs was already negotiated.

headline: Delhi high court to hear today Saurav Das’s plea seeking travel nod to UK
summary: Saurav Das, co-convener of CJP, has taken his case to the Delhi High Court after being barred from traveling to the UK. His legal representation emphasized the urgent need for a hearing, arguing that a swift resolution could enable Das to participate in essential university events abroad. He reported being halted at immigration without any visible orders, claiming the travel ban relates to his scheduled discussions at UK institutions.

headline: Indian Women's Hockey team creates history, climbs to world no. 4 after Japan rout
summary: In a remarkable achievement, the Indian women's hockey team has climbed to World No. 4 in the recent FIH World Rankings. This success follows impressive wins against notable Asian rivals, including a historic 6-2 victory over China. The unbeaten streak they’ve maintained in the tournament has secured their place in the semi-finals, showcasing the tremendous growth of women's hockey in India over the past few years.

headline: Lamp not lit atop deepathoon, Supreme Court to hear contempt case
summary: The Tamil Nadu government has not complied with the Supreme Court's order regarding the Karthigai Deepam lamp lighting. This non-compliance may trigger contempt proceedings against the Madurai Collector, despite his apology. Various political parties and the Madurai district administration oppose the lighting of the lamp atop the deepathoon.

headline: Musk says 'impressive work by Google', as CEO Pichai shares Neon's new Day record
summary: Elon Musk has publicly praised Google's recent advancements in artificial intelligence, highlighting their Neon model and Antigravity platform. Sundar Pichai shared updates on Neon's new Day-1 usage record as well as the increase in Antigravity token usage. The daily token usage surged by 82% following the launch of Argon just six weeks ago.

headline: ‘Fighting against BJP or us?’ Congress slams Samajwadi Party over its list
summary: Congress MP Imran Masood expressed doubts about the intentions of Samajwadi Party during ongoing seat-sharing negotiations. The discussions, which lasted 3.5 hours, were complicated by SP's announcement of five candidates, causing tension. Masood emphasized that Congress seeks a significant number of seats for the 2027 elections while supporting Akhilesh Yadav for CM.

headline: Minnesota neighbour posts no-access sign, moors boat; court upholds $64k fees
summary: A Minnesota couple sued their neighbour after he put up a sign claiming they had no harbour access and parked his boat along their waterfront, disrupting their attempts to sell two properties. An appeals court ruled that their property titles expressly granted water access, upheld findings of slander of title and nuisance, and confirmed a $64,061 attorney-fee award.

headline: Supreme Court nixes Allahabad HC order for Rahul’s assets probe
summary: Supreme Court has quashed an order from the Allahabad high court to investigate Rahul Gandhi's assets. The high court did not consider Gandhi's response before issuing the order, which raised procedural concerns. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal criticized the order, claiming it permitted a witch-hunt without examining the petitioner's standing.

headline: Chemistry most popular subject after English for 12th CBSE students
summary: In 2027, the CBSE has achieved an impressive milestone with 19 lakh candidates registering for Class 12. An encouraging trend reveals a marked rise in science registrations, notably in chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Notably, the disparity between chemistry and business studies has skyrocketed since 2019.

headline: Bengal’s new business model to draw from Maharashtra, Gujarat & UP, says Suvendu
summary: CM Suvendu Adhikari announced plans to replicate the industrial policies of Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat. The state government aims to restore confidence among industrialists to attract investments. Alongside these policies, a land bank is being created, addressing previous challenges in land acquisition.

headline: Florida jury awards $6m after man dies in neck surgery without cardiac clearance
Coimbatore teen who acted with Rajinikanth launches software firm with friends
summary: At just 13 years old, Rithvik Jothi Raj, who gained recognition from his performance in Jailer, has embarked on an exciting software journey with friends. What started as a conversation on video calls blossomed into a website showcasing products and courses. With interests ranging from coding to robotics and comic book writing, Rithvik is venturing into diverse areas, all while navigating the realms of acting and technology.

headline: Odisha girl, 10, becomes state's youngest known certified junior scuba diver
summary: At just 10 years old, Tvisha Panigrahi from Dubai, with roots in Odisha, has made waves by earning her Junior Open Water Diver certification. She completed her training a mere two days after her birthday, outshining her sister's prior achievement. With both her father and sister also certified divers, the family has truly embraced the diving adventure.

headline: 7th high court posting? Justice Rao may be Karnataka Chief Justice
summary: Justice M S Ramachandra Rao has been recommended for the position of Chief Justice of the Karnataka high court. This potential appointment would mark his seventh high court assignment since 2012 when he became a judge. He has previously served as Chief Justice in four high courts over a short period.

headline: India tops in videos removed from YouTube
summary: YouTube took down approximately 34.4 lakh videos from India in the second quarter of 2026. This number represented a 28% increase from the previous quarter's removals. Globally, child safety issues were responsible for the majority of video removals.

headline: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ foundation received $1.7 million from 28 funders
summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies received over a million from over 25 funders for their foundation between 2019 and 2025. Kansas City Chiefs owner Clark Hunt’s foundation and the league foundation are some of the funders who believe in Chiefs ace quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ vision for underserved children.

headline: Michael Misa makes a 22-year-old cancer survivor's NHL dream come true
summary: The San Jose Sharks helped an Illinois cancer survivor fulfil his dream of meeting favourite player Michael Misa during a family trip to California. Through the Sharks Foundation and goalie coach Thomas Speer, the young fan watched practice, met players and received signed gifts from Misa. The heartwarming experience gave him and his family lasting memories beyond the game.

headline: India urges B'desh to probe minority violence, says Hasina's return a separate matter
summary: In response to escalating violence against minorities in Bangladesh, India has expressed its serious concerns, urging the government there to conduct an extensive investigation. The Ministry of External Affairs noted the unique circumstances surrounding Sheikh Hasina's passport and extradition request, highlighting that these matters are being processed according to established protocols. Furthermore, two Indian nationals suffered injuries in a recent Houthi assault in Riyadh, prompting a strong condemnation from India.

headline: Pilot trainers face minimum flying-experience norm following spate of accidents

summary: Indian exporters are adapting to potential tariffs from the United States while they finalize a trade agreement. The impact of these tariffs may create temporary uncertainty for exporters as they manage future orders. Current strategies involve rushing shipments to avoid increased costs before the new tariffs kick in.

headline: Cabinet ministers advised to avoid foreign travel; Parliament meet likely by Dec 15
summary: Cabinet ministers have been advised to avoid international travel as Parliament may be convened before mid-December. The government aims to introduce a Constitution amendment bill for women's reservation during the next session. This proposal, linked with delimitation, could expand Lok Sabha's strength significantly.

headline: Meta meets Congress: Party challenges suspended accounts; company cites govt orders
summary: In New Delhi, Meta representatives held discussions with Congress social media officials amid growing complaints about account suspensions and content deletions affecting the opposition. Supriya Shrinate raised critical concerns about what she deemed interference by Meta in political issues. In response, the officials clarified that they strictly comply with Indian content laws and maintain their stance of political impartiality throughout these processes.

headline: ‘Our artists bringing new perspectives to art’: PM Modi after Venice Biennale award
summary: The India Pavilion received the Visitors’ Lion Award for Best National Participation at the Venice Art Biennale. Curated by Amin Jaffer, it featured five contemporary artists exploring themes of memory and migration. Prime Minister Narendra Modi acknowledged this achievement as a significant moment for India’s cultural landscape.

headline: Election Commission: Rectify wrong roll entries during SSR via Form
summary: Form 8 is being used for rectifying inaccuracies in the electoral roll during the special summary revision. Booth-level officers will verify mismatched entries to ensure accurate voter information collection. Electors can flag incorrect details, and booth-level officers must confirm these.

headline: Bail to be granted under UAPA when there is delay in trial, says Supreme Court
summary: The Supreme Court has confirmed that its authority to grant bail cannot be overridden by stringent laws. It ruled in favor of a government doctor who has been jailed for over four years. Additionally, the Court granted bail to senior officials involved in a significant corruption case in Rajasthan.

headline: Beant Singh assassin Rajoana seeks Rajiv Gandhi's killer-like relief after 30 years
summary: Balwant Singh Rajoana, who has been incarcerated for over three decades, is seeking mercy to have his death sentence reduced. His appeal references the recent release of AG Perarivalan, a former death row inmate turned lawyer. Senior counsel Mukul Rohatgi stresses Rajoana's transformation during imprisonment, while the Centre, represented by ASG KM Nataraj, counters that Rajoana's historical anti-constitutional statements warrant denial.

headline: Missing businessman's non-bailable warrant cancelled in AJL case, ED to move HC
summary: A special MP/MLA court in Rouse Avenue cancelled a non-bailable warrant against businessman Dinesh Pandey. The Enforcement Directorate is surprised and plans to appeal this decision in the Delhi high court. Pandey is reportedly involved in transferring Rs 10.4 crore through a shell company to Associated Journals Ltd. The court criticized the investigating officer for using a sealed cover, which is typically standard practice.

headline: Omar government breaks silence on Sheshnag row, says lake safe
summary: The J&K government asserted that Sheshnag Lake remains completely safe following allegations of construction by the Border Roads Organisation. Forest minister Altaf Kaloo reported that heavy machinery operated away from the lake, ensuring no soil entered the water body. A 12-member inspection team found no tampering with the lake's track as maintenance is performed before the Amarnath Yatra.

headline: Vande Mataram at J&K waqf event sparks row
summary: Several Muslim clerics who attended a Waqf Board event in Srinagar expressed their regret after Vande Mataram was played. They said their participation did not endorse the song, and they prayed for forgiveness. The song sparked controversy as it allegedly conflicts with Islamic principles of Tawheed, promoting the oneness of Allah.

headline: PM Modi wants ITI courses aligned with industry needs, jobs closer to home
summary: PM Narendra Modi emphasized the need for public sector undertakings to establish connections with Industrial Training Institutes. He highlighted the importance of a 'Classroom–Company–Career' approach to enhance employment opportunities for youth. Modi suggested that PSUs should evaluate future manpower needs and strengthen partnership with ITIs to recruit trained candidates.

summary: India's sugar production for the 2026-27 season is expected to decrease by 15%, primarily due to weather issues. Maharashtra and Karnataka will contribute significantly to the decline following inadequate rainfall. The expected net sugar production will be around 265 lakh tonne, down from nearly 280 lakh tonne last season.

Efforts to trace voters categorized as absent, shifted, deceased, or duplicate have seen limited success due to various challenges.

headline: PM Modi reviews infra projects worth over Rs 78k crore, stresses timely execution
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi led a review meeting on key infrastructure projects worth over Rs 78,000 crore. The discussion included strategies to enhance road, railway, power, and coal sectors while addressing delays and implementation issues. A significant focus was placed on improving the Industrial Training Institute ecosystem through the PM-SETU initiative.

He has come forward to admit violations of the company’s code of conduct, including multiple relationships. His approach to management has been under fire, particularly concerning Nvidia's ties with China.

headline: 25% penalty or 17% 'relief' with rider: What Trump's new tariff threat means for India

Up to 25% tariffs on all goods from India, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods would be applicable, but there is also the prospect of 17% tariffs if a trade deal is agreed on.

headline: Diesel price dips below Rs350 after 4 months; petrol rate down by Rs4

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs314 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) at Rs348 per litre on Nov 26 (Thursday). The prices of HSD and petrol have gone below the July 18 rate of Rs354.35 and Rs316.15 per litre, respectively.

headline: PIA passengers in UK left distressed as 2 flights cancelled due to abrupt Norse Atlantic suspension
summary: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) said on Wednesday it will move its UK operations to its own Boeing 777 fleet from Nov 26 after wet-lease partner Norse Atlantic Airways abruptly suspended operations, forcing the cancellation of two flights from London and Manchester. The development came after Norse Atlantic, a long-haul budget carrier, said its financial situation is “critical” and it requires new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

headline: KP’s Karak reports 'first polio case in 6 years', taking countrywide 2026 tally to 10
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication (NEOC) has confirmed the country’s 10th paralytic polio case of the year, with the latest infection from Karak district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. According to an official of the polio programme, the affected child is a 14-month-old girl from the district’s Shnawa Gudi Khel union council. The case is the first reported from Karak in six years, and the eighth of the year from KP, according to NEOC.

On Wednesday, three people were killed and 14 others injured when the under-construction building — reportedly being constructed illegally on a residential plot — collapsed.
